s: Applying the balance, Mathews held that terminating Social Security disability benefits does not require a pre-termination evidentiary hearing.
Disability determinations rest on documentary medical evidence, and benefits are not need-based as welfare is.
The core requirements are notice and an opportunity to be heard "at a meaningful time and in a meaningful manner."
Other elements depend on context: a neutral decisionmaker (Caperton v. A.T. Massey, 2009, on campaign contributions and recusal), confrontation, counsel, and a statement of reasons.
Hamdi v. Rumsfeld applied Mathews to a citizen held as an enemy combatant, requiring notice of the factual basis and a fair opportunity to rebut it before a neutral decisionmaker.
